title: Advancing the partially sorted prefix by a cycle
statement: Let $p$ be a natural number, let $\sigma,\tau,\rho$ be permutations of $\mathrm{Fin}(p+2)$, and let $a$ be a position. Suppose $\tau$ satisfies the partial sorting filter [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators] at a, and $\rho$ agrees with $\sigma$ at positions below a+1 and is strictly increasing at positions at least a+1. Write $b=\tau^{-1}(\sigma(a))$. Deleting position b+1 from the junction map [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators] gives $\rho$. Moreover $\rho=\tau\circ(a\; a+1\;\ldots\; b)^{-1}$, where the interval cycle fixes positions outside the interval and is identity when b=a.

source.place: Tag 01FM, cohomology-equation-first-homotopy, tail-labelled part of the omitted verification

proof.text: Injectivity of sigma and the fixed-prefix condition imply b>=a. Set c=Fin.cycleIcc a b and pi=tau*c.symm. The inverse cycle fixes k<a and k>b, sends a to b, and sends a<k<=b to k-1. These formulas follow by applying c and using Mathlib Fin.cycleIcc_of_lt, Fin.cycleIcc_of_gt, Fin.cycleIcc_of_last and Fin.cycleIcc_of_ge_of_lt.

The formulas show that pi agrees with sigma through a. In its remaining tail the argument of tau is i-1 up through b and i thereafter. These arguments are increasing and at least a, so pi has increasing tail. Apply unique partial sorting at stage a+1 to identify pi with rho.

Evaluate the junction composed with (b+1).succAbove at k. For k<a it is tau(k)=sigma(k); at a it is sigma(a)=tau(b); for a<k<=b it is tau(k-1); for k>b it is tau(k). Thus the deleted tuple equals pi and hence rho. All cases include b=a and the last a, when the advanced tail is empty.

lean.statement:
theorem cechPartialSort_advance (p : ℕ) (σ τ ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)))
    (a : Fin (p + 2)) (hτ : cechPartialSort σ τ a)
    (hρ : (∀ k, k.val < a.val + 1 → ρ k = σ k) ∧
      (∀ i j, a.val + 1 ≤ i.val → i < j → ρ i < ρ j)) :
    cechJunction σ τ a ∘ (τ.symm (σ a)).succ.succAbove = ρ ∧
      ρ = τ * (Fin.cycleIcc a (τ.symm (σ a))).symm
